judgements.justification: Both area chairs followed their reviewers' scores: A's cited 'no one strongly in favor', B's accepted on four ratings of 6 or more.
Neither recommendation rested on a forecast of impact beyond the paper; B praised breadth across tasks the paper actually ran.
The rebuttal moved three B reviewers up (tbWn, Rugm, kHDT) while no A score changed after it.

B's Reviewer_7vAs gave a 7 on two sentences of praise after three hours as 'not an expert', while A's Reviewer_41qE spent 12 hours testing the novelty claim; A's own thin review (La4a) was discounted.
Only A showed that CoPE is Pi-Net on the concatenated input and that bolded CIFAR10 gains lie within the run-to-run spread, and both counted against the paper.
Both committees saw the closeness to Pi-Net; A judged it a set of design choices, B read it as 'a natural continuation' and 'significant novelty'.
No score moved because of reviewer discussion; B's raises cite the authors' response and A's scores never moved.
No rating contradicts its own text: La4a's 7 matches its generic praise, and the low A scores match their criticisms.
B's unsure reviewer (7vAs) gave a clear 7, not a borderline score, and A's reviewers were confident.
A's area chair followed the three agreeing detractors, not one outlier; B's followed the mean.
The verbal assessments differed: A's reviewers argued against novelty and significance, B's praised them.
B's spotlight did not rest on unanimity without a high score; Rugm rated 8, and A's lower tier came from a lower mean.
kHDT raised on rebuttal tables whose 'Pi-net' super-resolution row is Pi-Net-SICONC and whose BigGAN row repeats SNGAN's FID, and that table is not in the camera-ready.
B's meta-review says all reviewers found the work 'useful and novel', the opposite of kHDT's 'a straightforward follow-up', and carries no weakness forward.
B's 7vAs rated 7 on 'clear improvements over baselines', which Tables 3 and 4 refute for CIFAR10; A's oDAB misread SNGAN's FID, though that point fed A's scores less.
The authors did not dispute Rugm's point that Karras et al. beat CoPE on conditional CIFAR10, and Rugm still raised to 8 as 'fully addressed'.
41qE's 2021-08-27 objection restated an earlier point and the authors answered it on 2021-08-29; no new objection came too late to answer.
The two committees' reviews differed in score and argument, so the split is not one tier threshold applied to identical reviews.
A's area chair followed the most careful reviewer (41qE); in B no reviewer reached a contrary expert verdict that the area chair passed over.
B's concerns were requests for details, metrics and comparisons that the rebuttal met, while A's core concern, novelty over Pi-Net, no response could fix and the authors conceded it.
La4a's 7 was A's outlier, but A stayed below threshold with or without it; no single score set either tier.
La4a never replied, but its high score was not one the response had answered; it simply stood unrevised and was discounted.
No area chair set aside a low outlier while defending acceptance.
No reviewer on either committee raised audience breadth or venue fit.
B's meta-review says 'one reviewer raising their score' when three did, and claims unanimous agreement on novelty that kHDT did not share.
A's Mncu, oDAB and La4a never answered the authors' response, so pre-rebuttal scores stood, while three B reviewers engaged and raised.
B's 7vAs said 'I am not an expert in this field' at confidence 3 yet gave a 7, which B's area chair counted in the 7.0 mean behind the spotlight.
A's reviewers did not split evenly; three of four rated below threshold.

reasoning: Both committees saw that CoPE is close to Pi-Net and lacks state-of-the-art baselines, but weighted that closeness differently (R06). Only A tested the novelty claim and the significance of the gains (R05); its core objection could not be answered by a rebuttal, while B's requests could (R20). The rebuttal lifted three B scores and none in A (R03), partly on rebuttal tables that do not hold up (R13) and despite an undisputed stronger result in Karras et al. (R16); A's reviewers mostly left the response unanswered (R26). B's spotlight counted a thin, non-expert 7 built on a wrong reading of the results (R04, R15, R27), and its meta-review misstated the reviewers' positions and dropped their weaknesses (R14, R25). Every cause in this pair fits an existing reason, so none was added.
